claims.text: Systematically varying the relative concentrations of magnetic elements can tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Compositional tuning can optimize the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
High-entropy alloys based on 3d transition metals have promising magnetic characteristics.
The initial non-equiatomic 3d-transition-metal HEA is a single-phase alloy.
The initial alloy has inherent lattice distortions.
Changing elemental ratios alters local chemical disorder and lattice distortions.
Local chemical disorder and lattice distortions modify interatomic distances and magnetic exchange couplings.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations can induce sizable magnetic moments in Co, Cr, and Ni within CoCrFeMnNi.
Changing elemental ratios alters the distribution and strength of magnetic moments.
Changing elemental ratios alters spin-fluctuation dynamics.
Composition-induced changes in exchange interactions, moments, and spin dynamics shift the magnetic ordering temperature.
Composition-induced changes in exchange interactions, moments, and spin dynamics modulate the magnetocaloric effect.
A compositionally tuned HEA will exhibit a shifted magnetic transition temperature at a targeted operating temperature.
A compositionally tuned HEA will exhibit an enhanced or optimized isothermal entropy change or adiabatic temperature change.
Composition-based tunability is limited to ranges that preserve a single-phase solid solution.
Excessive compositional changes may induce secondary phases that obscure or degrade the desired magnetic behavior.
